climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Cabernet Franc, Gewürztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Franc sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 8°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
